meta.homeTitle: DHMS — a content manager for your AI helper
meta.homeDescription: Manage what your AI helper knows and must do, in plain words. Free, in any language, on every device.
meta.howDescription: You manage your helper's knowledge, instructions and checks in plain words. DHMS writes the files your AI tool needs.

home.title: A content manager for your AI helper
home.lede: Tell your AI helper what it needs to know and what it must never do, in your own words. DHMS takes care of the rest.
home.problem1: An AI helper works well only when it knows your work: your facts, your way of doing things, and your limits. Today, setting that up means learning technical files that most people never see.
home.problem2: So most people just chat. Their chats quietly change their setup, and they never learn what changed or why. When the helper does not have clear knowledge, it guesses, again and again.
home.idea1: DHMS lets you manage your helper in plain words: what it should know, how it should work, and what it must never do.
home.idea2: DHMS turns that into the correct files for each AI tool you use. You never need to learn their names.
home.who1: People in any field: a marketing team, a law firm, a support desk, a clinic, a writer.
home.who2: Developers can use it too, but DHMS is not built only for them.
home.promiseFreeText: No price. The goal is to help people, not to sell.
home.promiseLanguageText: Every word on screen can be translated, including languages written right to left.
home.promisePlatformText: On the web, on Windows, macOS and Linux, and on iPhone and Android phones.
home.promiseSimpleText: No setup questions to start, and no technical words.

how.title: How it works
how.lede: You manage the content. DHMS writes the files your AI tool needs.
how.analogyTitle: Like websites, but for AI helpers
how.analogy1: At first, making a website meant writing code. Then website builders let anyone make one. Then content managers let people manage only the words and pictures, and pick any design.
how.analogy2: DHMS does the same for AI helpers. You manage what your helper knows and does. Your AI tool plays the part of the design.
how.knowledgeText: What your helper should know. Write it, or upload your documents.
how.rolesText: Who does which part of the work.
how.workflowsText: The order your helper follows for a task.
how.checksText: What your helper must always do, or must never do.
how.output1: DHMS writes the correct files for each AI tool, so you never have to.
how.output2: It tells you which checks your AI tool will enforce and which ones are only advice.
how.output3: It shows a check working: it tries to break your rule, and shows that it was stopped.
how.output4: It notices when your chats change your setup, and shows you what changed and why.
how.output5: It keeps your knowledge linked to where it came from, and tells you when the original changes.
how.note: These are the goals for DHMS. The product is still being researched.

status.title: Status
status.lede: DHMS is in research. No product code exists yet.
status.evidence1: Before building, we are collecting facts: what each AI tool can really do, what people use today, and where people who do not write code get stuck.
status.evidence2: Every fact has a source, a date and a date to check it again.
status.bar1: DHMS should be better than every other option. Before we build, we turn that into numbers: how fast someone gets a working helper, how often they finish a task, and how plain every word is.
status.code1: The code will be public. This page will link to it when it is.
